title: Long Pressed Name
notes:
Task and constraints: Return true if typed can be produced from name by long-pressing some characters, causing repeated characters in typed.
Idea: `isLongPressedName` advances through `name` when the current typed character matches; otherwise it accepts only a repeat of the previous typed character.
Technique and why it applies: Two pointers distinguish matching required characters from extra copies caused by long presses.
Invariant: The `i` pointer advances only when the next required name character is matched, and `j` consumes every typed character exactly once.
Edge cases: An extra repeat is valid only after a typed character exists; success also requires all characters of `name` to be consumed.
Complexity: O(n+m) time for both strings and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity_reason: Two pointers distinguish matching required characters from extra copies caused by long presses.

title: Long Pressed Name
notes:
Task and constraints: Return true if typed can be produced from name by long-pressing some characters, causing repeated characters in typed.
Idea: `isLongPressedName` advances through `name` when the current typed character matches; otherwise it accepts only a repeat of the previous typed character.
Technique and why it applies: Two pointers distinguish matching required characters from extra copies caused by long presses.
Invariant: The `i` pointer advances only when the next required name character is matched, and `j` consumes every typed character exactly once.
Edge cases: An extra repeat is valid only after a typed character exists; success also requires all characters of `name` to be consumed.
Complexity: O(n+m) time for both strings and O(1) auxiliary space.
code: class Solution { public boolean isLongPressedName(String name,String typed){int i=0,j=0;while(j<typed.length()){if(i<name.length()&&name.charAt(i)==typed.charAt(j)){i++;j++;}else if(j>0&&typed.charAt(j)==typed.charAt(j-1))j++;else return false;}return i==name.length();} }
complexity_reason: Two pointers distinguish matching required characters from extra copies caused by long presses.

title: Unique Email Addresses
notes:
Task and constraints: Count unique email addresses after ignoring dots and everything after + in each local part; domains remain unchanged.
Idea: Split each address at `@`, discard the local-part suffix beginning at `+`, remove dots from the remaining local part, and store the normalized address in a set.
Technique and why it applies: Normalizing only the local part before set insertion merges equivalent addresses without changing domains.
Invariant: The set contains one representative for each distinct address after local-part normalization; the domain is kept unchanged.
Edge cases: Dots and plus suffixes are ignored only before `@`; distinct domains remain distinct; valid email formatting is assumed.
Complexity: O(total email characters) time and O(number of normalized addresses) space.
complexity_reason: Normalizing only the local part before set insertion merges equivalent addresses without changing domains.

code:
import java.util.*;
class Solution { public int numUniqueEmails(String[] emails){Set<String>s=new HashSet<>();for(String e:emails){String[]p=e.split("@",2);String local=p[0].split("\\+",2)[0].replace(".","");s.add(local+"@"+p[1]);}return s.size();} }
complexity_reason: Normalizing only the local part before set insertion merges equivalent addresses without changing domains.

title: Number of Recent Calls
notes:
Task and constraints: Implement RecentCounter.ping(t), returning the number of calls in the inclusive interval [t-3000,t].
Idea: `ping(t)` appends the timestamp to a deque/queue and removes timestamps strictly less than `t-3000`; the remaining size is the inclusive-window count.
Technique and why it applies: A FIFO queue can discard expired calls from the front while retaining every timestamp inside the inclusive 3000ms window.
Invariant: After pruning, every stored timestamp lies in `[t-3000,t]`, and call timestamps remain in nondecreasing order.
Edge cases: The lower boundary `t-3000` is included; repeated calls are counted separately; old calls are removed from the front.
Complexity: Each timestamp is inserted and removed at most once, so calls are O(1) amortized and O(n) total storage in the worst case.
complexity_reason: A FIFO queue can discard expired calls from the front while retaining every timestamp inside the inclusive 3000ms window.

title: Number of Recent Calls
notes:
Task and constraints: Implement RecentCounter.ping(t), returning the number of calls in the inclusive interval [t-3000,t].
Idea: `ping(t)` appends the timestamp to a deque/queue and removes timestamps strictly less than `t-3000`; the remaining size is the inclusive-window count.
Technique and why it applies: A FIFO queue can discard expired calls from the front while retaining every timestamp inside the inclusive 3000ms window.
Invariant: After pruning, every stored timestamp lies in `[t-3000,t]`, and call timestamps remain in nondecreasing order.
Edge cases: The lower boundary `t-3000` is included; repeated calls are counted separately; old calls are removed from the front.
Complexity: Each timestamp is inserted and removed at most once, so calls are O(1) amortized and O(n) total storage in the worst case.
code:
import java.util.*;
class RecentCounter {Queue<Integer>q=new ArrayDeque<>();public RecentCounter(){}public int ping(int t){q.add(t);while(q.peek()<t-3000)q.remove();return q.size();}}
complexity_reason: A FIFO queue can discard expired calls from the front while retaining every timestamp inside the inclusive 3000ms window.

title: Reorder Data in Log Files
notes:
Task and constraints: Place all letter logs before digit logs; sort letter logs by content then identifier, while keeping digit logs in original order.
Idea: Split logs into letter and digit groups, sort letter logs by content and then identifier, and append digit logs in their original order.
Technique and why it applies: Separating log types allows the required sorting of letter logs without disturbing digit-log order.
Invariant: The letter group is ordered by the required two-key comparator, while digit entries preserve input order.
Edge cases: A letter log's identifier breaks equal-content ties; digit logs are never sorted; each log has an identifier and content.
Complexity: O(n log n) time for sorting and O(n) space for the two groups.
complexity_reason: Separating log types allows the required sorting of letter logs without disturbing digit-log order.

title: Reorder Data in Log Files
notes:
Task and constraints: Place all letter logs before digit logs; sort letter logs by content then identifier, while keeping digit logs in original order.
Idea: Split logs into letter and digit groups, sort letter logs by content and then identifier, and append digit logs in their original order.
Technique and why it applies: Separating log types allows the required sorting of letter logs without disturbing digit-log order.
Invariant: The letter group is ordered by the required two-key comparator, while digit entries preserve input order.
Edge cases: A letter log's identifier breaks equal-content ties; digit logs are never sorted; each log has an identifier and content.
Complexity: O(n log n) time for sorting and O(n) space for the two groups.
code:
import java.util.*;
class Solution { public String[] reorderLogFiles(String[] logs){List<String>letters=new ArrayList<>(),digits=new ArrayList<>();for(String x:logs){String rest=x.substring(x.indexOf(' ')+1);if(Character.isDigit(rest.charAt(0)))digits.add(x);else letters.add(x);}letters.sort((a,b)->{String ar=a.substring(a.indexOf(' ')+1),br=b.substring(b.indexOf(' ')+1);int c=ar.compareTo(br);return c!=0?c:a.substring(0,a.indexOf(' ')).compareTo(b.substring(0,b.indexOf(' ')));});letters.addAll(digits);return letters.toArray(new String[0]);} }
complexity_reason: Separating log types allows the required sorting of letter logs without disturbing digit-log order.

title: Range Sum of BST
notes:
Task and constraints: Return the sum of node values in a BST that lie in the inclusive range [low, high].
Idea: Add the current node value only when it lies in `[low,high]`; recurse left only if `root.val > low` and right only if `root.val < high`.
Technique and why it applies: BST ordering lets the method skip a left or right subtree when its values cannot enter the requested range.
Invariant: The returned subtotal includes every in-range node in the explored subtree; BST ordering safely excludes branches that cannot contain eligible values.
Edge cases: A null node contributes zero; both bounds are inclusive; pruning depends on the BST ordering invariant.
Complexity: O(n) worst-case time and O(h) recursion stack space.
complexity_reason: BST ordering lets the method skip a left or right subtree when its values cannot enter the requested range.

title: Range Sum of BST
notes:
Task and constraints: Return the sum of node values in a BST that lie in the inclusive range [low, high].
Idea: Add the current node value only when it lies in `[low,high]`; recurse left only if `root.val > low` and right only if `root.val < high`.
Technique and why it applies: BST ordering lets the method skip a left or right subtree when its values cannot enter the requested range.
Invariant: The returned subtotal includes every in-range node in the explored subtree; BST ordering safely excludes branches that cannot contain eligible values.
Edge cases: A null node contributes zero; both bounds are inclusive; pruning depends on the BST ordering invariant.
Complexity: O(n) worst-case time and O(h) recursion stack space.
code: class Solution { public int rangeSumBST(TreeNode root,int low,int high){if(root==null)return 0;int total=root.val>=low&&root.val<=high?root.val:0;if(root.val>low)total+=rangeSumBST(root.left,low,high);if(root.val<high)total+=rangeSumBST(root.right,low,high);return total;} }
complexity_reason: BST ordering lets the method skip a left or right subtree when its values cannot enter the requested range.

title: Valid Mountain Array
notes:
Task and constraints: Return true if an array strictly increases to one peak and then strictly decreases, with both sides non-empty.
Idea: Walk strictly uphill, reject if the climb has no step or reaches the last index, then walk strictly downhill and require the scan to end at the array boundary.
Technique and why it applies: Separate strict ascent and descent scans enforce one interior peak with both slopes present.
Invariant: The first loop stops at the unique candidate peak; the second loop succeeds only if every remaining adjacent pair decreases strictly.
Edge cases: Plateaus invalidate the strict comparisons; arrays shorter than three cannot have both nonempty sides.
Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
code:
class Solution:
 def validMountainArray(self,arr):
  n=len(arr);i=0
  while i+1<n and arr[i]<arr[i+1]:i+=1
  if i==0 or i==n-1:return False
  while i+1<n and arr[i]>arr[i+1]:i+=1
  return i==n-1
complexity_reason: Separate strict ascent and descent scans enforce one interior peak with both slopes present.

title: Delete Columns to Make Sorted
approach_name: Check each column top to bottom
notes:
Task and constraints: Count columns that are not sorted in nondecreasing order from the first row to the last row.
Idea: For each column, compare adjacent rows and increment the answer once at the first descending pair in that column.
Technique and why it applies: Adjacent comparisons detect whether each column is sorted, and a break counts each offending column once.
Invariant: A column contributes one deletion if and only if some adjacent row pair violates nondecreasing order.
Edge cases: An empty list returns zero; equality is allowed; the inner loop breaks after finding a bad pair to avoid double counting.
Complexity: O(rows × columns) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity_reason: Adjacent comparisons detect whether each column is sorted, and a break counts each offending column once.

title: Delete Columns to Make Sorted
approach_name: Check each column top to bottom
notes:
Task and constraints: Count columns that are not sorted in nondecreasing order from the first row to the last row.
Idea: For each column, compare adjacent rows and increment the answer once at the first descending pair in that column.
Technique and why it applies: Adjacent comparisons detect whether each column is sorted, and a break counts each offending column once.
Invariant: A column contributes one deletion if and only if some adjacent row pair violates nondecreasing order.
Edge cases: An empty list returns zero; equality is allowed; the inner loop breaks after finding a bad pair to avoid double counting.
Complexity: O(rows × columns) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
code: class Solution { public int minDeletionSize(String[] strs){if(strs.length==0)return 0;int ans=0;for(int c=0;c<strs[0].length();c++)for(int r=1;r<strs.length;r++)if(strs[r].charAt(c)<strs[r-1].charAt(c)){ans++;break;}return ans;} }
complexity_reason: Adjacent comparisons detect whether each column is sorted, and a break counts each offending column once.

title: Verifying an Alien Dictionary
approach_name: Compare adjacent words by custom ranks
notes:
Task and constraints: Return true if the list of words is sorted according to a supplied alien alphabet order.
Idea: Build a rank lookup from the alien alphabet and compare each adjacent pair of words at their first differing character.
Technique and why it applies: A custom rank table makes first-difference comparisons follow the supplied alphabet rather than ordinary character order.
Invariant: The first differing character decides lexical order; if one word is a prefix of the other, the shorter word must come first.
Edge cases: Only adjacent pairs need checking; equal words are valid; a longer word preceding its exact prefix is invalid.
Complexity: O(total characters) time and O(1) space for the fixed alphabet rank table.
complexity_reason: A custom rank table makes first-difference comparisons follow the supplied alphabet rather than ordinary character order.

title: Verifying an Alien Dictionary
approach_name: Compare adjacent words by custom ranks
notes:
Task and constraints: Return true if the list of words is sorted according to a supplied alien alphabet order.
Idea: Build a rank lookup from the alien alphabet and compare each adjacent pair of words at their first differing character.
Technique and why it applies: A custom rank table makes first-difference comparisons follow the supplied alphabet rather than ordinary character order.
Invariant: The first differing character decides lexical order; if one word is a prefix of the other, the shorter word must come first.
Edge cases: Only adjacent pairs need checking; equal words are valid; a longer word preceding its exact prefix is invalid.
Complexity: O(total characters) time and O(1) space for the fixed alphabet rank table.
code: class Solution { public boolean isAlienSorted(String[] words,String order){int[]rank=new int[26];for(int i=0;i<order.length();i++)rank[order.charAt(i)-'a']=i;for(int i=1;i<words.length;i++){String a=words[i-1],b=words[i];int j=0;while(j<a.length()&&j<b.length()&&a.charAt(j)==b.charAt(j))j++;if(j==b.length()&&a.length()>b.length())return false;if(j<a.length()&&j<b.length()&&rank[a.charAt(j)-'a']>rank[b.charAt(j)-'a'])return false;}return true;} }
complexity_reason: A custom rank table makes first-difference comparisons follow the supplied alphabet rather than ordinary character order.

title: N-Repeated Element in Size 2N Array
notes:
Task and constraints: An array of length 2N contains N+1 distinct values, with one value repeated N times; return that repeated value.
Idea: Scan values while adding unseen values to a set; return immediately when a value is already present.
Technique and why it applies: A seen set detects the repeated element at its second occurrence without building full frequencies.
Invariant: The set contains exactly the distinct values from the processed prefix, so the first duplicate encountered is the specially repeated value under the problem guarantee.
Edge cases: The array guarantee ensures a duplicate exists; the fallback return is only defensive in the Java implementation.
Complexity: O(n) expected time and O(n) space.
complexity_reason: A seen set detects the repeated element at its second occurrence without building full frequencies.

code:
import java.util.*;

title: Univalued Binary Tree
approach_name: Check every node against the root value
notes:
Task and constraints: Return true if every node in a binary tree has the same value.
Idea: Traverse nodes with a stack and compare every node's value to the root value, returning false on the first mismatch.
Technique and why it applies: Comparing every reachable node against one reference value directly verifies the tree's univalued property.
Invariant: Every visited node matches the root value until a mismatch is found; exhausting the stack proves all values agree.
Edge cases: A null root returns true in the Python version; leaf nodes add no children; the traversal avoids recursion.
Complexity: O(n) time and O(h) to O(n) stack space depending on tree shape.
complexity_reason: Comparing every reachable node against one reference value directly verifies the tree's univalued property.

title: Univalued Binary Tree
approach_name: Check every node against the root value
notes:
Task and constraints: Return true if every node in a binary tree has the same value.
Idea: Traverse nodes with a stack and compare every node's value to the root value, returning false on the first mismatch.
Technique and why it applies: Comparing every reachable node against one reference value directly verifies the tree's univalued property.
Invariant: Every visited node matches the root value until a mismatch is found; exhausting the stack proves all values agree.
Edge cases: A null root returns true in the Python version; leaf nodes add no children; the traversal avoids recursion.
Complexity: O(n) time and O(h) to O(n) stack space depending on tree shape.
code:
import java.util.*;
class Solution { public boolean isUnivalTree(TreeNode root){if(root==null)return true;ArrayDeque<TreeNode>q=new ArrayDeque<>();q.push(root);while(!q.isEmpty()){TreeNode n=q.pop();if(n.val!=root.val)return false;if(n.left!=null)q.push(n.left);if(n.right!=null)q.push(n.right);}return true;} }
complexity_reason: Comparing every reachable node against one reference value directly verifies the tree's univalued property.
